summary.overview: Papagaio has strong project-owned mechanisms — a checksum-pinned runtime bootstrap shared by local dev, GitHub Actions, and Xcode Cloud, plus focused behavior-level tests on the core pipeline — but they are not fully wired together: the only setup/navigation entrypoint is being deleted while in-code references still depend on it, the remaining first-run instructions contradict the repository's canonical truth, and the app-layer test sources are attached to no build or CI gate. This was a session-limited review: no eligible sessions were available in the 30-day window, so all behavior claims rest on inspected project mechanisms only.

dimensions.label: Task Understanding
dimensions.summary: A README and unusually rich Package.swift boundary rationale currently route setup and architecture context, but the current change deletes that entrypoint while comments still reference it, and no session evidence exists to show the route is actually used.

dimensions.label: Controlled Execution
dimensions.summary: bootstrap-runtimes.sh is a strong, checksum-pinned, loud-failing setup route reused by CI and Xcode Cloud, but the documented first-run story contradicts it (stale Git LFS steps and a nonexistent workspace name), and no doctor or reset surface exists.

dimensions.label: Change Validation
dimensions.summary: PapagaioCore has dense, focused Swift Testing coverage with negative and recovery cases and a filtered fast route, but the PapagaioTests sources are wired to neither the Xcode project nor CI, leaving the highest-churn SwiftUI layer without any mechanical check.

dimensions.label: Reliable Delivery
dimensions.summary: Recent history shows an active PR-based acceptance practice with per-PR CI on main, but merge-enforcement is host-side and unverified, and the current change set sits unstaged directly on main.

dimensions.label: Learning Capture
dimensions.summary: The review window contains no eligible session episodes (source roots disabled or missing), so repeated work, friction, and reuse opportunities cannot be detected; no durable learning owner is configured and no later outcome exists.

findings.title: Deleting the only setup and navigation docs leaves the project without a task entrypoint and dangling architecture references
findings.reason: The current unstaged change deletes README.md and Master Plans/DECISIONS.md on main, while PapagaioCore/Package.swift comments still route readers to them ("Ver DECISIONS.md", decisions D-3.1/D-3.2). If committed as-is, agents and humans lose the only documented setup order, test command, and contribution route, and the package's boundary rationale points at files that no longer exist. Fact: verified via git diff --name-status and Package.swift lines 14/60. Uncertainty: the deletion may be an intentional reorganization in progress, and the content is recoverable from git history; no agent-instruction file (AGENTS.md/Rules) exists to absorb the route.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Document owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Restore or replace the project's task entrypoint before the deletion lands: either keep a concise README (setup order, test command, contribution route) or move the still-referenced decision records to a new owner, then update the Package.swift comments that say "Ver DECISIONS.md" to point at the surviving route.

## Validation

- Grep the repository for references to deleted files (README.md, DECISIONS.md, PROMPT-MESTRE.md) and confirm none remain dangling
- Confirm one document routes first-run setup, the PapagaioCore test command, and the PR practice

findings.title: Fresh setup following the README hits wrong LFS steps and a workspace file that does not exist
findings.reason: README.md (HEAD) instructs `git lfs install && git lfs pull`, claiming the frameworks in PapagaioCore/Frameworks/ are versioned via Git LFS, but .gitattributes is empty and .gitignore keeps PapagaioCore/Frameworks/ out of git; Scripts/bootstrap-runtimes.sh is the canonical download route and its header records that the script and LFS previously disputed ownership of the same artifacts. The README also tells the reader to open "Papagaio.xcworkspace", which does not exist (the project opens via Loro.xcodeproj). Anyone cloning HEAD today follows steps that describe a repository state that no longer matches reality. Uncertainty: the README is slated for deletion in the current change, so this consequence may be transient; no fresh-clone run was executed in this review.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Document owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Reconcile the first-run story with canonical truth: inspect Scripts/bootstrap-runtimes.sh, .gitignore, and .gitattributes, then replace the stale Git LFS instructions and the nonexistent "Papagaio.xcworkspace" reference with the actual setup order (bootstrap script, then open Loro.xcodeproj), or fold the corrected steps into whatever document replaces the README.

## Validation

- Every setup step in the surviving entrypoint matches the current .gitignore/.gitattributes and bootstrap script behavior
- The named project file to open exists in the repository

findings.title: App-layer tests exist but run in no build or CI gate, so regressions in the fastest-changing SwiftUI layer merge silently
findings.reason: PapagaioTests/ contains two test files (BibliotecaTests.swift, InterfaceTests.swift, ~340 lines), but Loro.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj contains zero references to PapagaioTests (verified at HEAD and in the working tree) and .github/workflows/ci.yml only runs `swift test` in PapagaioCore plus an app build that never executes tests. Meanwhile the project's hottest churn sits in SwiftUI views (ArquivoDetalheView, CartaoDeConversa, BibliotecaHomeView) and ViewModels/Biblioteca.swift — exactly the app layer with no mechanical feedback. This is a verified wiring gap: declared test sources, an active CI entrypoint, and no connection between them. Uncertainty: the app tests may have been intended for a local scheme or Xcode Cloud pipeline that was not inspected; whether CI is a required check is host-side and unverified.
expectedOutput: Update the existing Config owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Decide the fate of PapagaioTests and wire the chosen route end to end: inspect Loro.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj, the Loro scheme, and .github/workflows/ci.yml, then either attach PapagaioTests as a real test target of the Loro project and add an `xcodebuild test` step to CI, or explicitly retire the orphaned test files.

## Validation

- Run the wired app-test route locally once and confirm it discovers PapagaioTests
- Confirm the same route executes in .github/workflows/ci.yml (or confirm the deliberate retirement)
